verdict: No concrete static blocker in the exact finite adaptations. Actual binding, preservation snapshots and assembled packet remain later root-owned evidence.

check-preservation.py.addition: Exact sourceCommit HEAD equality for both S and Q before clean/index snapshot claims.

preservation.purpose: An explicitly invoked read-only snapshot with one exclusive private result file; it does not restore source or run product checks.
preservation.protectedInputSelection: The preferred post-repair file has 113 byte/hash pins. Its historical sourceHead is not used as current HEAD; the future binding sourceCommit is checked for both S and Q.
preservation.boundSource: Every boundPaths relative source is read under both S and Q and compared by exact length/SHA. The actual future row count and commit are not validated by this static review.
preservation.native: The path-deduplicated union of protected native pins, existing binding natives and fresh native is checked against resolved physical path, dev/inode, link count1, bytes and SHA. Root’s future binding review must ensure duplicate path rows agree and the actual six native identities remain distinct; this helper does not itself assert pairwise distinctness.
preservation.state: Both S/Q HEAD values must match binding sourceCommit, both statuses and indexes must be empty. Held R status/head and empty index must match the retained exact snapshot.
preservation.target: The fresh RFC target uses lstat regular/single-link/canonical-path checks and an inode different from S. Those are finite path-based observations, not an atomic descriptor or continuous-isolation proof.
preservation.claimBoundary: Result flags are emitted only after the preceding assertions. No unrecorded earlier physical check, runtime native-load identity, descendant isolation or whole-history claim is added.

assembler.purpose: Assembles only a root-supplied finite manifest into a new exclusive private dated directory. It is not the semantic source/runtime/receipt validator.
assembler.adaptation: Private base, P1-26 dated directory/key and tree-qualification branch only; the date and all other assembly logic are unchanged.
assembler.closedCommands: Requires unique nonempty phase selection, matching phase, endedUtc, recorded ESRCH/no nonzero signals and exact borrowed-R cwd/head. Actual cmd/exit/duration triples are preserved, including closed failures; no exit normalization or synthetic future command is added.
assembler.sourceAdoption: Sources must be files and not final-component symlinks; supplied expected bytes/SHA are checked before adoption. Destinations reject absolute paths/traversal and use exclusive writes. Output artifacts have exact SHA entries.
assembler.lossless: Logs and explicitly selected artifacts use base64 JSON envelopes with original path/bytes/SHA and an immediate strict decode equality check. No original bytes or command result are edited.
assembler.rules: Each emitted artifact is capped at1,048,576 bytes. The forbidden private-key marker is checked both before optional encoding and on emitted bytes. These finite rules are not generic secret detection or full schema/filename validation.
assembler.inertTestEvidence: No helper-level inert-suffix assertion is present. The future root-owned manifest must target candidate test copies only under inert filenames or the established lossless JSON envelope. The actual packet must be reviewed/validated before source adoption. This is the already required caller boundary, not approval for executable qualification copies.
assembler.helperSource: The assembler contains its own literal forbidden-marker guard. Keep it pinned by path/bytes/SHA; do not adopt its source or encode it as an artifact to evade the guard.
assembler.trustedManifest: Root still owns exact semantic review of source commit, environment, tests, notes, artifact inventory, target names and actual runtime/control masks. The helper does not derive those claims or independently verify all outcome semantics.
assembler.futureValidation: No assembler invocation, packet creation, manifest adoption, schema-validator result, freeze/staging/commit or final receipt success is claimed here.

rootSourceCheckpoint.boundary: The checkpoint record is pinned as input; no new Git/source command or broad quality verification ran in this review.

holds: All Claude work, held R rows/index/archive, missing reservation binding, F37 skip, public-entry approval and remaining whole-issue/library/P1-25 decisions are preserved.
execution: Text/JSON/hash/diff metadata reads and private review writes only. Neither helper, product, compiler, test, native addon, SQL, network or process probe was executed; no source/index/Git/QA writes occurred.
